description:
Add a flatten-extras catch-all field to every public Deserialize struct that appears on the JMAP wire, AND add forward-compat Unknown(String) variants to wire-format **result** string enums, so vendor/site/private extension fields and unrecognised result-enum values round-trip losslessly. Today the workspace silently drops unknown fields on deserialize and most string enums fail to deserialize unknown variants outright.

## Stated motivation

Implementors and sites add custom data fields (and likely custom enum variants) to JMAP types without waiting for IETF process (Mark, 2026-05-09). RFC 8620 §1.6 mandates silent-ignore of unknown fields on deserialize but is silent on preservation. Spec floor allows data loss; production reality requires preservation.

## Two coordinated mechanisms (all in this epic)

### Mechanism 1: `extra` field on structs

    #[non_exhaustive]
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    pub struct Email {
        pub id: Id,
        // ... typed fields ...

        /// Catch-all for vendor / site / private extension fields not
        /// covered by the typed fields above. Preserves unknown fields
        /// across deserialize/serialize round-trip per workspace policy.
        #[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]
        pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
    }

Wire format byte-identical when extras are empty (skip_serializing_if).

### Mechanism 2: `Unknown` variant on **result** string enums

    #[non_exhaustive]
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    pub enum MailboxRole {
        Inbox,
        Sent,
        // ... known RFC 8621 §2.1.1 variants ...

        /// Forward-compat catch-all for vendor / site / future-spec roles.
        /// The wire string is preserved for round-trip.
        #[serde(other)]
        Unknown(String),
    }

Wire format unchanged for known variants. Unknown wire values now deserialise into Unknown(s) instead of failing. Note: `#[serde(other)]` only captures the *variant tag* — the matched value is the original string. The chat-types ephemeral.rs already uses this once; this epic generalises it to result enums (MailboxRole, DeliveryState, NodeType, EmojiKind, ChatKind, ParticipantRole, etc.). Control enums (Operator, ComparatorProperty) are explicitly excluded — see "Decision: filter algebra excluded" below.

## Scope (every public Deserialize struct OR result-enum that appears on the JMAP wire)

In scope:
- Data object types and their nested wire sub-types (Email + EmailAddress + EmailHeader + …, Calendar + CalendarEvent + jscalendar typed sub-types, ContactCard + jscontact typed sub-types, Task + tasks typed sub-types, Chat + Message + Space + nested, FileNode, Principal, etc.).
- Standard response wrappers (GetResponse<T>, SetResponse<T>, ChangesResponse, QueryResponse, QueryChangesResponse).
- Method-argument structs in client crates (EmailSubmissionSetParams, MailboxSetParams, etc.).
- Wire-format **result** string enums get Unknown(String) variants (MailboxRole, DeliveryState, NodeType, EmojiKind, ChatKind, ParticipantRole, etc.).

Out of scope:
- **Filter and comparator algebra types in every crate** (Filter<T>, FilterOperator<T>, EmailFilterCondition, MailboxFilterCondition, CalendarEventFilterCondition, EmailComparator, etc.). DECIDED OUT 2026-05-10 — see "Decision: filter algebra excluded" below.
- **Control string enums** (Operator, ComparatorProperty, etc.) — DECIDED OUT 2026-05-10 — see same. These remain `#[non_exhaustive]` so RFC-level forward-compat is preserved without a vendor-level `Unknown(String)` escape hatch.
- Internal Rust API types: backend trait result types (SetDefaultResult, ParseResult, AvailabilityError, BackendSetError, BackendChangesError, etc.).
- MockBackend state structs, FaultyBackend, NoSnippetBackend, TrackingBackend.
- tests/common/* helper types.
- Internal parsing helpers, dispatcher types, MIME tree types.
- jmap-types::PatchObject (already a Map<String, Value>; redundant).
- Property selector enums (server-side; not on the wire).
- Newtypes wrapping a single value (Id, UTCDate, Date, State, Keyword).

## Decision: filter algebra excluded (2026-05-10)

The original epic listed filter and comparator algebra as in-scope ("Mechanism 3"). On 2026-05-10 this was reversed. Three reasons:

1. **Silent-drop foot-gun at the server.** Unlike data-object extras (which round-trip mechanically through the client), an unknown filter condition like `{"acmeCorpPriority": "high"}` means nothing unless the server understands and indexes it. A query that silently drops a filter clause is a P0 query-correctness bug. With extras the client compiles and serialises a clause the server may silently ignore — no compile-time signal, no runtime trap, wrong result set returned.

2. **`Filter<T>` is `#[serde(untagged)]` over a fixed set of variants.** Adding `extra` to the fields of `EmailFilterCondition` would not let a vendor add a third variant-shape (e.g. a new operator-shaped node). That mechanism would have to come from extending the `Operator` enum, which is itself a control enum and falls under reason 3.

3. **Control enums must dispatch on known variants.** `Operator` (AND/OR/NOT) and `ComparatorProperty` are not display values — backends must implement matching logic for each variant. `Unknown(String)` is meaningless here: a backend cannot honor `XAND` or `someUnknownSortKey`. The `#[non_exhaustive]` derives already give spec-level forward-compat (RFCs add new operators); vendor-level forward-compat for control enums is incoherent.

Vendors who need filterable extras have two paths:

- **IETF-track**: use `draft-ietf-jmap-metadata` (currently draft-01, capability URI `urn:ietf:params:jmap:metadata`). It defines a companion Annotation object keyed by `(relatedType, relatedId)` with schema discovery via the capability's `dataTypes` / `metadataTypes` / `maxDepth` properties and a `Metadata/query` filter (currently `textMatch` over vendor string properties). This is the IETF answer to exactly the gap the filter-algebra exclusion identifies: extras with capability declaration and a real filter operation. Workspace implementation tracker: JMAP-06zp.
- **Pre-IETF escape**: vendors who need typed filter construction RIGHT NOW (before the metadata draft stabilises) can fork the per-crate FilterCondition type or use `serde_json::Value` for the filter tree — the hybrid sloppy-value pattern (per `crate-jmap-calendars-types/PLAN.md`) is the right escape hatch for that case.

Neither path uses the workspace extras pattern. The exclusion holds.

## Field/variant shape (decided 2026-05-09)

Struct extras:
- Name: `extra` (matches existing MethodResponseError.extra precedent in jmap-types).
- Type: `serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>`.
- Visibility: pub field.
- Attributes: `#[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]`.

Result-enum forward-compat:
- Variant: `Unknown(String)`.
- Attribute: `#[serde(other)]`.
- All in-scope enums remain `#[non_exhaustive]`.

Per-type tests required for both mechanisms (round-trip preservation for structs; deserialize-unknown-variant + round-trip for result enums).

## Order dependency (decided 2026-05-09)

This epic depends on JMAP-sehw (contacts jscontact.rs typed sub-types) and JMAP-yfpq (tasks jstask / shared jscalendar) landing first. Rationale: sehw and yfpq introduce many NEW typed sub-types; landing them before this epic lets this epic sweep across them in one pass, rather than landing this epic first and then having to remember the policy retroactively when sehw/yfpq land.

bd dep links: this epic depends on sehw and yfpq.

## Decomposition

Per-crate children, each one a self-contained migration in lock-step with the canonical-template propagation rule (workspace AGENTS.md): when the canonical jmap-mail-types adopts the pattern, every extension-types sibling adopts the same shape in the same pass.

  .1 jmap-types               (foundation type crate)
  .2 jmap-mail-types          (canonical extension-types template)
  .3 jmap-chat-types          (extension-types sibling; also normative for JMAP Chat draft)
  .4 jmap-calendars-types     (extension-types sibling)
  .5 jmap-contacts-types      (extension-types sibling)
  .6 jmap-tasks-types         (extension-types sibling)
  .7 jmap-filenode-types      (extension-types sibling)
  .8 jmap-sharing-types       (extension-types sibling)
  .9 *-client crates (method param structs)
  .10 workspace AGENTS.md update

Each child covers BOTH mechanisms (extras on data structs, Unknown(String) on result enums) for its crate. Children .2 through .8 already exclude filter/comparator algebra in their out-of-scope lists; child .1 was updated 2026-05-10 to record the decision. When a child is claimed, the implementer expands the field-and-enum-by-field list from the crate's source files.

## Coordination with existing epics

- JMAP-sehw (contacts jscontact.rs typed sub-types): blocks this epic. Land sehw first; this epic sweeps the new types when it runs.
- JMAP-yfpq (tasks jstask / shared jscalendar): blocks this epic. Same.
- JMAP-pmpa, JMAP-s0p5, JMAP-78lb (per-field PatchObject migrations on notification structs): orthogonal; can land before or after this epic.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every in-scope public Deserialize struct has `extra` with the documented attributes.
- Every in-scope wire-format **result** string enum has `Unknown(String)` with `#[serde(other)]`.
- Filter/comparator algebra types and control string enums (Operator, ComparatorProperty) remain unchanged — they are explicitly out of scope per the 2026-05-10 decision.
- Every in-scope type has at least one round-trip preservation test.
- Workspace AGENTS.md documents the policy AND the filter-algebra exclusion rationale.
- Every migrated crate's PLAN.md notes the policy in the type-design section.
- `cargo test --workspace` clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.
- Wire format byte-identical for empty-extras / known-variant case (verified by tests against existing fixtures).

## Open design questions

- Property serialization order: confirmed via test that serde_json::Map preserves insertion order under workspace's serde_json feature config; if not, switch to indexmap-based map.
- Typo masking in caller code: doc warning, not enforced.
- JMAP using[] discipline: not enforced at the type level; consumer responsibility.
- Hash/Eq semantics for Unknown(String): some enums currently derive Eq/Hash for use as HashMap keys. Adding Unknown(String) is fine for Eq/Hash since String is Eq/Hash. Verify each enum's existing derive chain still compiles.

## Cookie-cutter coordination

Children .1 (jmap-types), .2 (jmap-mail-types), and .3 (jmap-chat-types) touch the foundation and canonical extension-types crates. Per the canonical-template propagation rule in workspace AGENTS.md, .2 (the canonical extension-types template) must land in lock-step with all six extension-types siblings (.3 chat, .4 calendars, .5 contacts, .6 tasks, .7 filenode, .8 sharing) — either as a single sweep or with a follow-up sweep bead before the canonical change is merged. The substantive question for each child is "have I covered every wire-shaped type in the crate" (per cookie-cutter completeness), not "is approval needed".

## Status

Epic and 10 children filed 2026-05-09. **Mechanism 3 (filter algebra) dropped 2026-05-10 — children .2-.8 already aligned via their out-of-scope sections; parent description corrected; child .1 updated to remove the "needs design discussion" hedge.** PAUSED until JMAP-sehw and JMAP-yfpq land. Resume with JMAP-lbdy.4 (calendars-types) once sehw/yfpq are closed.
title: EPIC: workspace-wide extras-preservation policy (round-trip for vendor/site fields)
